To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HuR overexpression stabilizes ARE‐containing reporter mRNAs, HuR deletion mutants that lack the third RRM do not stabilize ARE‐containing RNAs, HuR shuttling is demonstrated in HeLa–L cells heterokaryons.

HuR, a member of the El av family of RNA‐binding proteins, is localized in the nucleus and shuttles between nuclear and cytoplasmic compartments, and overexpression of Hu R increases the in vivo half‐life of mRNAs containing AU‐rich elements.
HuR is an important regulator of ARE‐mediated mRNA degradation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a new RNA‐binding protein, HuR, and its function in the ARE‐dependent mRNA decay pathway.
the identification and characterization of proteins that bind to the AU‐rich elements in mRNA 3′ UTRs.
the identification and characterization of HuR, an RNA binding protein that is involved in the ARE‐dependent decay of mRNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ARE‐mediating decay pathway is a two‐step process: (i) HuR binds to AREs in the nucleus, and (ii) HuR‐bound AREs in the cytoplasm are targeted for degradation by a cytoplasmic protein.
overexpression of the HuR protein increases the stability of ARE‐dependent mRNA transcripts in vivo.
HuR overexpression increases mRNA stability by protecting the ARE‐containing mRNA from cytoplasmic deadenylation and degradation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HuR is a nuclear protein that can be shuttled to the cytoplams and that overexpression of this protein stabilizes the ARE‐containing RNAs.
HuR is a nuclear–cytosolic shuttling protein which is important for mRNA decay and is likely to play a role in the regulation of proto‐oncogene and cytokine mRNA stability.
HuR is an ARE‐specific RNA binding protein that can stabilize ARE‐containing RNAs in vivo and that it may function in both the nucleus and cytosol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HuR is an RNA binding protein that can stabilize ARE‐containing transcripts in vivo.
HuR is a positive regulator of ARE‐contained mRNAs and that HuR is an RNA binding protein that shuttles between nucleus and cytoplasma.
HuR, a member of the Elavl/RBD family, is a positive regulator of mRNA stability in vivo.
